A noun case used to express means or agency—and is generally indicated in English by by or with with the objective. Languages that use the instrumental case include Armenian, Serbo-Croatian, Czech, Dyirbal, Georgian, Latvian, Slovene, Polish, Ukrainian, Quechua, Russian, Assamese, Tamil, Turkish and Sanskrit. Extinct languages that used the instrumental case include Old English, Old Saxon and Old High German.

glosses: Essential or central; of great importance or relevance.

examples.text: He was instrumental in conducting the business.
The head is not more native to the heart, The hand more instrumental to the mouth

glosses: Serving as an instrument, medium, means, or agency.

examples.text: Maxwell started back to his study, feeling that kind of satisfaction which a man feels when he has been even partly instrumental in finding an unemployed person a remunerative position.
